n: Jeremiah wishes his head were a spring of water and his eyes a fountain of tears so he could weep day and night for his slain people. This verse is why he’s called “the weeping prophet.” (In Hebrew Bibles this is 8:23.)

f.w: Oh that my head were waters

n: In the same breath, he wishes he had a traveler’s shack in the desert so he could get away from them all—a band of unfaithful traitors. Love and frustration mix in his heart.

f.w: a lodging place of wayfaring men
f.g: A rough desert inn for travelers.
Unfaithful—both literally and in breaking covenant with God.

n: They bend their tongues like bows to shoot lies. They aren’t courageous for truth; they go from one evil to another and don’t know God.

f.w: they are not valiant for the truth

n: Be careful of your neighbor; don’t trust even your brother—every brother is a deceiver like Jacob, and every friend a slanderer. Trust has collapsed.

f.g: A wordplay on Jacob’s name: “every brother will Jacob-ize”—cheat and trip up.

n: They deceive their neighbors and never speak the truth. They’ve trained their tongues to lie and wear themselves out doing wrong.

f.w: taught their tongue to speak lies

n: You live surrounded by deceit, and through deceit they refuse to know Me.
So God will refine and test them like metal in a furnace—what else can He do for His people?

f.w: I will melt them, and try them

n: Their tongue is a deadly arrow. A man speaks friendly words to his neighbor while secretly setting an ambush.

f.w: one speaketh peaceably to his neighbour with his mouth

n: God repeats: shouldn’t I punish this? Shouldn’t I avenge Myself on such a nation?
Jeremiah (or God) mourns for the mountains and pastures, scorched so no one passes through. No cattle lowing, birds and animals gone—an eerie silence.
Jerusalem will become a heap of ruins and a home for jackals; Judah’s towns will be empty.
Who is wise enough to understand this? Who has heard from God and can explain why the land is ruined like a desert?
The Lord answers: because they abandoned My law and didn’t obey My voice.
They followed their own stubborn hearts and the Baals their fathers taught them. False traditions passed from parents to children.
So God will feed them wormwood and give them poisoned water—bitterness and suffering.

f.g: A very bitter plant, a symbol of sorrow and bitterness.

n: He will scatter them among nations they never knew and send the sword after them. The scattering of Israel was foretold by Moses.

f.w: I will scatter them also among the heathen

n: Call for the professional mourning women—the skilled ones—to come. Ancient funerals employed women trained in lament.

f.g: Professional mourners who led public weeping.

n: Let them hurry and wail for us until our eyes run with tears.
A cry is heard from Zion: “How we are ruined! We are deeply ashamed, for we’ve left our land and our homes have been torn down.”
Women, hear God’s word: teach your daughters to wail and one another a funeral song. So many will die that more mourners will be needed.
Death has climbed in through the windows and entered the palaces, cutting down children in the streets and young men in the squares. Death is pictured as a thief or invader.

f.w: death is come up into our windows

n: Bodies will lie like dung in open fields, like stalks left behind a reaper that no one gathers.

f.g: Bundles of cut grain left behind by a reaper.

n: One of Jeremiah’s best-known teachings: the wise shouldn’t boast in their wisdom, the strong in their strength, or the rich in their riches.

f.w: Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom

n: Instead, let anyone who boasts boast in this: that he understands and knows Me—that I am the Lord who shows steadfast love, justice, and righteousness, for these delight Me. Knowing God is life’s true treasure.

f.w: that he understandeth and knoweth me

n: The days are coming when God will punish everyone circumcised only in the flesh—outward sign without inward faithfulness.

f.g: Circumcised in body but uncircumcised in heart.

n: Egypt, Judah, Edom, Ammon, Moab, and desert tribes who clip the hair at their temples—they all practiced circumcision, but it means nothing. Judah, though circumcised, is “uncircumcised in heart.”

f.w: all that are in the utmost corners
f.g: Literally “those with clipped temples”—desert tribes who cut their hair at the sides.
